anomalies.observed: The P-channel MOSFET Q1 is connected with its source on the +5V rail and its drain on the USB-C VBUS input net: +5V includes Q1.2(S), while USBC_VBUS_IN includes Q1.3(D) and U6.1(VIN). U6.6(SENSE) is on +5V.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode/or-ing path from USB-C VBUS into the +5V rail, the P-MOSFET source should be on the USB input side (USBC_VBUS_IN/VIN) and the drain on the +5V/SENSE side, so the body diode and gate control block reverse current from +5V back into USB-C.
anomalies.impact: The ideal-diode orientation is reversed. When USB VBUS is absent or lower than +5V, Q1's body diode can conduct from +5V back into the USB-C VBUS net, defeating reverse-current protection and potentially back-feeding the USB-C port or preventing proper USB power OR-ing.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of LEDs D4, D14, and D23; it has no supply pin, driver pin, resistor to a rail, or other source.
anomalies.expected: A LED anode power net named /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW should be connected to a 3.3V supply or a switched 3.3V driver so that D4, D14, and D23 can light when their cathode-side signals are pulled low.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 cannot form a complete circuit and will remain off, removing the associated power/Ethernet status indications.

parsed.summary: The design files show two likely deviations: Q1 is source/drain reversed for the LTC4412 USB ideal-diode path, and the /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW LED supply net is left floating, so the related status LEDs cannot light.
